analysis:
The PR adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml), a changelog entry, and test pins in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache or fan-helper code. The canonical threat model (TB-002 through TB-013, A-001 to A-019, T-041 and others) covers the provider runtime and the sandbox-installer boundary, not CI scheduling, so no threat IDs apply.

I checked the workflow for concrete CI-side regressions:
- Top-level permissions are `{}`. The single job has only `actions: write` and `checks: write`. It uses no secrets, checkout, third-party actions or id-token. API calls go over HTTPS to `github.api_url` for `github.repository` only (lines 73-74, 97-101).
- Repository variables are validated: `minutes` must match a numeric regex and be 15 to 1440, and the repository name is regex-checked. Run and job data (job names, SHAs) come from the GitHub API. Job names are sanitised by `clean` (line 148) before reaching summaries or check-run text. jq uses `--arg` and `--argjson`, so there is no shell or jq injection.
- The watchdog acts only on runs with a queued Darkbloom-labelled job (`self-hosted` plus `darkbloom-*`, lines 145-146). The new test asserts that release, signing and credentialed workflows never carry such labels, so the cancel/re-run authority does not reach them. Re-run only replays the original workflow definition and does not escalate privilege.
- Marker check runs can be created by any holder of `checks: write`. Suppression is gated on `app.slug` equal to the configured Darkbloom app, and resume is gated on slug `github-actions` plus an exact title. A forged marker could at worst delay or skip a rescue, which is an availability nuisance with no confidentiality impact.
- The rescue is bounded to 2 per round, 12-minute timeout, 10-page pagination caps, and `concurrency` serialisation.

The test changes only widen the allowed-label checks for this one file by name. Residual uncertainty: the behaviour of GitHub-hosted APIs and of Darkbloom's own watchdog (the `Darkbloom watchdog` marker contract) is outside the supplied evidence.
